title: WHIRLPOOL_Malware_Investigation_11e
description: Investigate and respond to a WHIRLPOOL malware compromise on a Barracuda Email Security Gateway device.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Barracuda Email Security Gateway (ESG) device in your network has been compromised by the WHIRLPOOL malware, a Linux ELF reverse shell variant. Your task is to investigate and respond to this security incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the target host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: target
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content:
Investigate the target host for suspicious services or processes.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service running on port 4444? (Flag: service name)
levels.solution:
To find the suspicious service running on port 4444, use the following command:

```bash
sudo ss -tulnp
```

The name of the suspicious service running on port 4444 is `ssld.service`. This is the flag you need to submit. The flag type is a service name.

hints.title: Check running services
hints.content:
Check running services. Use the following command to list all services:

```bash
sudo systemctl list-units --type=service
```

hints.title: Check network connections
hints.content:
Check network connections. Use the following command to list all network connections:

```bash
sudo ss -tulnp
```

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service maintains persistence on the target host.

**Question:** What is the name of the systemd service unit file responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service? (Flag: service unit file path)
levels.solution:
To determine the persistence mechanism, use the following command:

```bash
ls /etc/systemd/system/
```

The name of the systemd service unit file responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service is `/etc/systemd/system/ssld.service`. This is the flag you need to submit. The flag type is a service unit file path.

hints.title: List systemd service files
hints.content:
List systemd service files. Use the following command to list all service files:

```bash
ls /etc/systemd/system/
```

hints.title: Examine the suspicious service file
hints.content:
Examine the suspicious service file. Use the following command to check the contents of the suspicious service file:

```bash
sudo cat /etc/systemd/system/ssld.service
```

levels.title: Investigate Malicious File
levels.content:
Investigate the file associated with the suspicious service.

**Question:** What is the name of the file that the suspicious service is using for its malicious activities? (Flag: file path)
levels.solution:
To investigate the file associated with the suspicious service, use the following command:

```bash
ls -la /home/cyrano/
```

The name of the file that the suspicious service is using for its malicious activities is `/home/cyrano/ssld`. This is the flag you need to submit. The flag type is a file path.

hints.title: List files in the home directory
hints.content:
List files in the home directory. Use the following command to list all files in the home directory:

```bash
ls -la /home/cyrano/
```

hints.title: Examine the suspicious file
hints.content:
Examine the suspicious file. Use the following command to check the contents of the suspicious file:

```bash
cat /home/cyrano/ssld
```
